recentItems.title: Brooklyn News Today: Woman assaulted in Prospect Park, body found in can, burglary probe
recentItems.description:
Brooklyn investigators are searching for a suspect after a woman was assaulted on a trail in Prospect Park, while police continue investigating the discovery of a woman's body inside a trash can at Plumb Beach in Sheepshead Bay. Authorities are also seeking suspects connected to pharmacy break-ins across the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens, a burglary involving more than $17,000 in sports trading cards, and a shooting investigation on 17th Avenue. Meanwhile, artists marked one year since a devastating Red Hook fire, the Met Council distributed kosher food ahead of the Jewish High Holidays, and city agencies launched the "Know Your Zone" emergency preparedness campaign.

recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Pharmacy thefts, DWI arrest and hit-and-run probe
recentItems.description:
A second person has died as health officials continue investigating a disease cluster in parts of Melrose and Morrisania, bringing the total to 14 reported cases. Police are searching for four people accused of stealing more than $60,000 in medication and cash during a series of break-ins targeting pharmacies and businesses in the Bronx, Brooklyn and Queens. Exclusive surveillance video shows a woman being struck by a vehicle in Soundview, where police say a person was arrested for driving while intoxicated. Authorities are also investigating a hit-and-run that seriously injured a cyclist in the South Bronx, while the city launches its new “Know Your Zone” campaign to encourage residents to prepare evacuation plans for severe weather events.

recentItems.title: Accused bathroom voyeur found in the Bronx after Norwalk City Hall bathroom recording
recentItems.description:
A woman told police that a man held a cellphone underneath a bathroom stall and appeared to be recording inside Norwalk City Hall. Detectives say surveillance footage helped identify 31-year-old Terrill Kelly as the suspect after he allegedly fled the area. Police later located Kelly in the Bronx and extradited him from Rikers Island back to Norwalk. Authorities say he is being held on a $50,000 bond and is due back in court on Sept. 29.

recentItems.title: Daughter speaks after 2 arrested in mother’s hit-and-run death
recentItems.description:
Two people have been arrested in the death of 49-year-old Zandrea Harris, who police say was struck and killed in a hit-and-run crash in Bridgeport, Connecticut. Investigators say Jahmeir Tillery and Ti Norfleet moved Harris while she was critically injured and failed to get her emergency medical care. Harris’ daughter says she is grateful arrests have finally been made and that justice is being served.

recentItems.title: The untold story behind an iconic Billy Joel 9/11 photo
recentItems.description:
One of the most memorable images from the days after 9/11 showed an FDNY helmet resting on Billy Joel’s piano during the America: A Tribute to Heroes concert. Photographer Kevin Mazur captured the historic moment but spent years wondering who the helmet belonged to. Two decades later, he finally met retired FDNY Lieutenant Neil Skow, the firefighter whose helmet became a symbol of sacrifice, remembrance, and dedication. Their reunion led to a touching recreation of the iconic image with Billy Joel at Madison Square Garden.

recentItems.title: Super El Niño could reshape WINTER: What it means for NY, NJ, CT
recentItems.description:
A powerful “Super El Niño” is developing, with much warmer-than-average waters in the equatorial Pacific helping reshape global weather patterns. The latest NOAA outlook suggests a stormier winter ahead, with the jet stream tracking over the tri-state area. While precipitation may increase, warmer temperatures could leave the region stuck in a rain-snow battleground rather than guarantee a snowier season.

recentItems.title: Connecticut News Today: Officer trial, Fairfield murder case and coyote attack
recentItems.description:

A judge found probable cause to prosecute Tahnyi Johnson in the 2022 killing of 15-year-old Zion Burton in Fairfield. Police are urgently searching for missing Milford resident Kellen Neely, while a Fairfield woman continues recovering after a coyote attack that led to the animal being euthanized.
